Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

jam

adverb

already, by now; in a moment (with a future); now (by now, at last); in a moment; have been (doing) since, for

In this lexicon

  • already

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Men. 2.3.86: jamne ībis?, are you going so soon? (Lewis & Short); Cic. Imp. Pomp. 52: obsolēvit jam ista ōrātiō (Lewis & Short)

  • in a moment

    also used · classical · Plaut. Cas. 526: jam hīc erō; Ter. Eun. 85: jam calēscēs; Traupman 88: soon (in a minute), jam

  • now

    also used · classical · Ter. And. 3.4.2: jam advesperāscit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 88: now, nunc; (denoting emphasis and urgency) jam

  • since

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.9.1: jam diū ignōrō quid agās

  • jam dūdum (jam diū): already

    classical

  • jam diū, jam dūdum (+ present): have

    classical

  • Cōnsequar jam tē!: I’m gonna get you!

    classical

Notes

  1. 1Write consonantal i as j in all Latin, quotations included: jam, ejus, major, conjungō, Jōannēs. Ruling: Consonantal i is written j.

Examples

  • Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.

    My mind’s been on the dishes for ages.Ter. Eun. 816

    In the entry for already

  • jam diū ignōrō quid agās; nihil enim scrībis

    I haven’t known how you are for a long time now; you don’t writeCic. Fam. 7.9.1

    In the entry for already

  • cūrā, ego ad forum modo ībō: jam hīc erō. — Bene ambulā.

    Look after things; I’m just going to the forum: I’ll be back in a moment. — Have a good walk.Plaut. Cas. 526

    In the entry for in a moment

  • hanc domum jam multōs annōs est quom possideō

    it is many years now that I have owned this housePlaut. Aul. prol. 4 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for since

  • jam diū ignōrō quid agās; nihil enim scrībis

    I haven’t known for a long time how you are, for you never writeCic. Fam. 7.9.1
